title: Normalized reconstruction of composites of completed operations
statement:
Let $A,I,P_n$, the constant pro-etale module categories $D(T,A)$, strict reduction functors $\mathcal R_T$, diagram categories $D(\mathcal T_T)$ and completion reflectors $C_T$ be as follows: $A$ is commutative Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated, $A/I$ is additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite and perfect for every $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]; $T$ ranges over schemes with the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$, and $\mathcal R_T(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ on its diagram site [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Write $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ for the total right derived inverse-limit functor and $C_T=\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_T$ with its specified completion unit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. All direct images and inverse images use the canonical derived adjunctions on these constant-module categories.

Consider a finite composable word $W_c=F_m\cdots F_1$ on complete objects, in which each $F_i$ is either completed inverse image $u_c^*=C_Uu^*$ for a scheme map $u:U\to V$, derived direct image $Ru_*$, or completed open extension $J_j^c=C_VJ_j$ for an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, lem-sf-cbc-extension-zero-completion]. Let $\widetilde F_i$ be respectively termwise inverse image $G_u$, total derived termwise direct image $R_u^{\mathcal T}$, or termwise open extension $J_j$, and put $\widetilde W=\widetilde F_m\cdots\widetilde F_1$. There are specified natural isomorphisms
$$q_{W,K}:\mathcal R(W_cK)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde W\mathcal R(K),\qquad a_{W,K}:W_cK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\widetilde W\mathcal R(K)).$$
For one letter, $q$ is the inverse of reduction of the completion unit followed by the strict pullback/tensor comparison, the diagram-site counit-tensor projection-formula map for direct image, or the map $q_{j,K}$ for completed open extension. For the empty word $q=1$ and $a$ is the complete object's completion unit. For a concatenation $VW$, the normalization is
$$q_{VW,K}=(\widetilde Vq_{W,K})\circ q_{V,W_cK},\qquad a_{W,K}=\mathcal L(q_{W,K})\circ\eta_{W_cK}.$$
Thus these are comparisons in derived strict-diagram categories, independent of parenthesization, not merely identifications of evaluated objects. For direct image, $a$ agrees with the canonical direct-image/derived-limit comparison normalized by tower projections [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. No uniform cohomological or Tor interval on $K$ or on intermediate objects is required; every assertion is in the ambient complete categories. No compactification, exchange-pasting equation, or faithfulness of derived evaluations is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ and use the diagram-site realization to regard strict towers as modules on one site. The tower category is abelian and its evaluations are exact, and the strict-tower homotopy-limit statement supplies the exact functor $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$. The completion adjunction identifies $C_TK$ with $\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_T(K)$ and supplies its unit $\eta_K$. For the empty word take $q_{1,K}=1$ and $a_{1,K}=\eta_K$.

source.place: Proof Step 5, strict-diagram prerequisite and empty-word normalization

proof.text: For a completed inverse-image letter $u_c^*=C_Uu^*$ with $u:U\to V$ and complete $K$ on $V$, put $M=Lu^*K$. By part (i) of the completed-pullback-unit-tower lemma, $\mathcal R_U(\eta_M)$ is an isomorphism in the derived strict-tower category, and by part (ii) the strict pullback/tensor comparison $\tau_{u,K}:\mathcal R_U(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_u\mathcal R_V(K)$ is a natural isomorphism of derived towers. Set $q_{u,K}=\tau_{u,K}\circ\mathcal R_U(\eta_M)^{-1}:\mathcal R_U(C_Uu^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_u\mathcal R_V(K)$; this is exactly the one-letter map of the statement and is natural in $K$. This uses no completeness assertion for the ordinary object $u^*K$. By part (iii) of that lemma, with the constant/completed coefficient equivalence and the definition of completed pullback, its level-$n$ components are the projection-induced isomorphisms $\alpha_n$ of the completed-pullback-reduction lemma, so $q_{u,K}$ is the tower form of the finite-reduction identifications used elsewhere. For successive inverse-image letters, the pro-etale derived-pullback-composition comparison on K-flat representatives identifies the strict composite $G_vG_u$ with the termwise pullback for the composite map.

For a derived direct-image letter $Ru_*$, with $u:U\to V$ and complete $K$ on $U$, the constant-tower direct-image-normalization lemma gives $\chi_{u,K}:\Delta(Ru_*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_u^{\mathcal T}\Delta K$, whose evaluations are identities. Let $h_{u,K}:\mathcal R_V(Ru_*K)\to R_u^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_U(K)$ be the diagram-site counit-tensor projection-formula map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] for the object $\Delta K$ and the coefficient tower $(\underline{P_n}_V)_n$, with source identified through $\chi_{u,K}$. Apply the completion-mate comparison lemma to the identity square ($g=\mathrm{id}_V$, $g'=\mathrm{id}_U$, $f=f'=u$, identity comparison isomorphism), which is permitted since that lemma imposes no hypothesis on the square and $K\in D_{\mathrm{comp}}(U,A)$. There $G_g$ and $G_{g'}$ are identity functors and the pullback/tensor identification is the identity, so its map $H$ is $h_{u,K}$; that lemma states that $H$ is invertible in the derived tower category and that its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical projection-formula isomorphism for the constant perfect coefficient complex $\underline{P_n}$. Set $q_{u,K}=h_{u,K}$; it is natural in $K$. For successive direct-image letters, the direct-image composition comparison for ringed topoi, applied termwise and to the constant towers through $\chi$, gives the normalized identification of $R_v^{\mathcal T}R_u^{\mathcal T}$ with the termwise direct image for the composite.

source.place: Proof Step 5, proper/direct-image generator and composition

proof.text: For a completed open-extension letter $J_j^c=C_XJ_j$, the extension-zero completion lemma supplies the normalized strict comparison $q_{j,K}:\mathcal R_X(J_j^cK)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_U(K)$, the equation $q_{j,K}\mathcal R_X(\eta_{J_jK})=q^{\rm tens}_{j,K}$, and the presentation $J_j^cK\cong R\lim(J_j\mathcal R_UK)$. These comparisons are natural and respect every quotient transition, so they may be composed with the comparisons for adjacent letters.

Proceed by induction on the length of the word. Suppose the normalized comparisons have been constructed for $W$ and let $V$ be one more letter. The strict comparison for $VW_c$ is the composite $q_{VW,K}=(\widetilde Vq_{W,K})\circ q_{V,W_cK}$; each factor is an isomorphism by the generator cases, and naturality makes the composite compatible with all tower transitions. Every $W_cK$ is complete: completed letters land in the complete subcategory by construction, and $Ru_*$ preserves complete objects by the completion adjunction lemma; hence $\eta_{W_cK}$ is the unit of a reflective subcategory at one of its objects and is invertible. Applying the exact functor $\mathcal L$ and then the completion unit gives the isomorphism $a_{W,K}=\mathcal L(q_{W,K})\circ\eta_{W_cK}$. The empty-word case starts the induction. Parenthesizing a finite formal word in different ways changes only the placement of the canonical associativity maps for composition of functors and natural transformations; their coherence is the ordinary associativity and functoriality of composition. Thus the construction is independent of parenthesization and natural in $K$.

source.place: Proof Step 5, compatibility with the compact-support composition law

proof.text: For the direct-image letter, let $i_{U,F}:\Delta F\to\mathcal R_U(F)$ be the strict quotient-unit map and let $h_{u,F}$ be the projection-formula map constructed above. The constant-tower direct-image-normalization lemma supplies the canonical isomorphism $\chi_{u,F}:\Delta(Ru_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_u^{\mathcal T}\Delta F$, its evaluation compatibility, the strict equation $h_{u,F}i_{V,Ru_*F}=R_u^{\mathcal T}(i_{U,F})\chi_{u,F}$, and the fact that the canonical comparison $a_{u,\Delta F}$ is the identity under the canonical constant-tower limit identifications. Let $a_{u,M}:Ru_*\mathcal L_U(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_VR_u^{\mathcal T}(M)$ be the canonical direct-image/derived-limit comparison and define $\rho_{u,F}=a_{u,\mathcal R_UF}^{-1}\mathcal L_V(h_{u,F})$. Applying $\mathcal L$ to the displayed strict equation, using naturality of $a_u$, the normalized identity for $a_{u,\Delta F}$ (part (3) of that lemma), and $\mathcal L(i_{U,F})=\eta_F$ (the completion unit of the completion adjunction lemma under $\mathcal L(\Delta F)\cong F$), gives the strict natural-transformation equation $$\rho_{u,F}\,\eta_{Ru_*F}=Ru_*(\eta_F).$$ This is obtained before evaluating the tower, so it does not infer equality of maps into $R\lim$ from their projections. Consequently the resulting $a$ is exactly the stipulated direct-image/derived-limit comparison. No uniform Tor or cohomological interval, compactification, or faithfulness of evaluations is used.
